classification.text_en: The Quran says there is no bird that flies on its two wings but it is a community like people.

origin.note_en: The Quran does not describe the origin of birds in general.

purpose.text_en: Everyone in the heavens and the earth glorifies God, and the birds in rows; each knows its prayer and its glorification.

nature.text_en: The birds above people in rows are held up by none but the Most Merciful.

abilities.text_en: Sulayman was taught the speech of the birds, and the birds were among his hosts. The birds were gathered with Dawud, each one turning back.

limitations.note_en: The Quran does not describe limits of birds in general.

relationship_with_humans.text_en: Ibrahim asked to see how God gives life to the dead so that his heart be at ease. He was told to take four birds, place a portion of them on each hill, and call them, and they would come to him in haste. The birds were subjected with Dawud, and Sulayman was taught their speech.

quranic_events.text_en: The four birds of Ibrahim; the hoopoe in Sulayman's account; the raven; birds in flocks against the companions of the elephant; a clay form of a bird that Isa says becomes a bird by God's permission; and, in Yusuf's prison, an interpretation that birds will eat from a head.

chronological_position.note_en: The Quran gives no time or order for birds as a group.

location.text_en: Birds are above people, in rows.

misconceptions.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the verse on Ibrahim's four birds asks him to take four and call them. It names no kinds of birds, and this profile names none.

lessons.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): birds appear as glorifiers, as held up by God, and as a means of easing Ibrahim's heart, which is read as a lesson that signs of God's power may be seen in ordinary creatures.

vocabulary.text_en: Words used: al-tayr (birds), mantiq al-tayr (the speech of the birds), saffat (in rows), tayran ababil (birds in flocks), awwab (turning back).
